basics.name: Roth design catalogues: Karlheinz Roth, 'Konstruieren mit Konstruktionskatalogen' (Designing with design catalogues, Springer, 3 volumes) and the guideline VDI 2222 Blatt 2 'Konstruktionsmethodik; Erstellung und Anwendung von Konstruktionskatalogen' (setting up and using design catalogues)
basics.url: Band 2 table of contents (3rd ed., German National Library/dandelon scan): https://external.dandelon.com/download/attachments/dandelon/ids/DE0048A7CC70CD50E5D1BC1257B48003FFDAB.pdf ; 1st edition (1982) contents: https://d-nb.info/810346869/04 ; Band 2 on Google Books: https://books.google.com/books/about/Konstruieren_mit_Konstruktionskatalogen.html?id=aCckBgAAQBAJ ; Band 3 (Verbindungen und Verschluesse): https://www.barnesandnoble.com/w/konstruieren-mit-konstruktionskatalogen-karlheinz-roth/1119170482 and https://openlibrary.org/books/OL12777361M.json ; VDI 2222 Blatt 2 at DIN Media: https://www.dinmedia.de/en/technical-rule/vdi-2222-blatt-2/549878
basics.resource_type: classification system and book (a multi-volume German handbook of systematic design catalogues, plus a VDI guideline on how such catalogues are built)
basics.cost: paid: Band 3 paperback $89.99 at Barnes & Noble; Band 1 and Band 2 are Springer print/eBook titles at similar prices (not verified) [uncertain]; VDI 2222 Blatt 2 PDF 120.60 EUR (print 134.30 EUR) from DIN Media

VDI 2222 Blatt 2: February 1982, now withdrawn

basics.image_license: All rights reserved (Springer figures and catalogue sheets)
basics.authority_level: academic / official standard: Roth was a leading figure in German design methodology, associated with TU Braunschweig (named in the Google Books term list; affiliation not checked on an opened page) [uncertain]; VDI 2222 Blatt 2 is an official VDI engineering guideline (now withdrawn)

coverage.covers: Band 2 (3rd ed.) holds 41 design catalogues, 210 figures with about 2,400 individual drawings and 516 term definitions. Catalogues relevant to connections and mechanisms: types of 'closure' (Schlussarten: form, force and material closure; element and combined closures), one-way and two-way stops, friction systems incl. self-clamping ones, variation of friction systems, logical pairing of solid bodies, mechanical logic gears (negation, AND/OR), mechanical flip-flops incl. push-push switches (T-flip-flops), generating force, single-stage force multipliers, mechanical backstops (one-way locks by friction clamping or positive contact, switchable backstops), chains and mechanisms up to four links, one-stage friction systems (wedge, lever and wrap-band systems), uniform-ratio gears with special tooth forms, fixed connections (rivets incl. blind rivets, shaft-hub connections), moving connections (linear guides incl. rolling-element guides, plain and rolling bearings), shape variation operations, forming processes, adhesive bonding of plates and cylinders, tolerance chains, plus a chapter on blocking motion with support points (Stuetzpunkte) and a directory of catalogues published by others. Band 3 covers connections and closures: classification of connections, catalogues of fixed connections, moving connections, function integration in connections and closing elements, systematics of combining connections, making fixed connections, and catalogues and a systematics of closures (Verschluesse, e.g. lids and latches)
coverage.organisation: Each catalogue follows the uniform structure set out by Roth and VDI 2222 Blatt 2: a classifying part (Gliederungsteil: rows/columns by physical principle, closure type, motion or geometry), a main part (Hauptteil: sketches of each solution) and an access part (Zugriffsteil: properties to filter and compare), with a 'Prinzipblatt' explaining each catalogue; catalogues are either overview or detail catalogues, and object, operation, solution or relationship catalogues. Chapters follow the design process (task formulation, function, principle, embodiment). Very systematic, but all in German engineering jargon and organised by abstract principle, so a beginner who does not know the terms would find it hard
coverage.scope_match: high for principle-level connection and mechanism types (closure types, backstops, stops, clamping friction systems, force multipliers, mechanical flip-flops, closures, shaft-hub joints), which match the project's 'clever types' scope; medium overall, because much is general design method, tolerancing and standard machine elements (rivets, bearings), and it is in German and paywalled
coverage.taxonomy_used: Classification by physical principle and by 'closure' (Schluss): form closure (Formschluss, positive locking), force closure (Kraftschluss, friction/force locking) and material closure (Stoffschluss, bonding), plus combined closures; connections split into fixed (feste) and moving (bewegliche) connections, and closures (Verschluesse) as a separate group; mechanisms by number of links and joint types (turning, sliding, two-way joints); a 'logical closure matrix' (Logische Schluss-Matrix) that records which directions of motion each body pairing blocks. Band 2 arranges its 41 catalogues in 14 topic sections (11.1-11.14), with support-point motion blocking as a separate chapter (13)
coverage.example_types: form-fit vs friction-fit vs bonded joints (Schlussarten); one-way stop (einseitiger Anschlag); two-way stop (zweiseitiger Anschlag); self-clamping friction system (klemmfaehiges Reibsystem); wedge system (Keilsystem); lever system; wrap-band system (Schlingbandsystem, wrap spring); single-stage force multiplier (e.g. toggle or lever amplifier) [uncertain]; mechanical backstop by friction clamping (Klemmschluss-Gesperre, freewheel-like); switchable backstop (umschaltbare Ruecklaufsperre); mechanical negation gear and AND/OR logic gears; mechanical RS flip-flop; mechanical T flip-flop / push-push switch (Tastschalter); special-tooth uniform-ratio gears (Sonderverzahnungen); blind rivet joints; shaft-hub connections; linear guides with rolling elements; secured, assemblable and dismountable rotary connections; window hinge designed automatically by computer; closures (Verschluesse) and closing elements [uncertain for Band 3 detail]
coverage.making_methods: General mechanical engineering and precision/fine-mechanism design (machining, forming, riveting, bonding); computer-aided and automatic design; nothing specific to 3D printing
coverage.item_count: Band 2 (3rd ed.): 41 design catalogues, 210 figures, about 2,400 individual drawings, 516 term definitions, 473 pages (Google Books). 1st edition 1982: 38 catalogues, 276 figures, about 3,000 drawings, 476 definitions. Band 3: about 256 pages with 177 figures (search summary only) [uncertain]. VDI 2222 Blatt 2: 43 pages
coverage.special_behaviours_covered: self-locking: yes (self-clamping friction systems, clamping backstops). One-way/ratchet: yes (mechanical backstops by friction clamping or positive contact, switchable backstops). Indexing / bistable: yes in the form of mechanical flip-flops and push-push switches. Force multipliers (toggle/lever amplification) and wedge/wrap-band friction systems. Gear trains: uniform-ratio gears with special teeth and 'developing different gears from the same mechanism'. Adhesives: a catalogue of bonded joint layouts for plate and cylinder parts (joint geometry, not adhesive chemistries). Closures and latches in Band 3 [uncertain in detail]. Not covered: torque-limiting (not seen in contents), hand-release only, over-centre (not named), compliant/flexure joints, print-in-place, powered connectors
coverage.entry_structure: A catalogue sheet: classifying columns/rows, a sketch of each solution principle, and access columns listing properties (e.g. direction of blocking, force transmission, can be undone), preceded by a 'Prinzipblatt' explaining how the catalogue is built; supporting text chapters with case examples (e.g. bolt-setting tool, hand riveting machine, corkscrew)
coverage.audience_level: professional and university (design engineers, mechanical engineering students and researchers)

usefulness.beginner_friendliness: low: German, dense technical terms (Schlussart, Elementenpaarung, Stuetzvektor), abstract principle drawings and matrix notation; valuable to an expert translating it, not to a beginner reading it directly
usefulness.has_images: yes: many small line sketches (about 2,400 in Band 2), schematic quality
usefulness.gaps: No English version; no photos, animations or plain explanations; no 3D-printing or maker guidance; standard machine elements dominate some catalogues; paywalled and not linkable per type; no compliant, print-in-place or powered connectors
usefulness.good_for_entry_links: poor: no per-catalogue web pages; only book-level records (Springer, Google Books, Open Library) and scanned tables of contents
usefulness.reusable_data: not reusable: print/eBook only, all rights reserved; the classification ideas (closure types, access-part properties) can be re-expressed in our own words and cited
usefulness.maintained: static: latest edition 3rd (2000-2001) with reprints around 2012; VDI 2222 Blatt 2 (1982) is marked withdrawn by DIN Media but still sold
usefulness.ideas_to_borrow: (1) Uniform entry structure: a classifying part, a main part with one sketch per solution and an 'access part' of comparable properties; our finder fields can play the role of the access part. (2) Classify every connection by how it holds: shape (form-fit), friction/force (force-fit) or bonding (material-bond), which gives a simple first flow-chart question. (3) Split fixed connections, moving connections and closures (latches, lids) into separate branches. (4) Catalogue families of clever mechanisms by function, e.g. 'stop motion in one direction', 'multiply force', 'lock against reverse motion', 'toggle on/off with a push'. (5) Overview catalogue leading to detail catalogues. (6) A table of which directions of motion a joint blocks (Roth's closure matrix, similar to degrees of freedom tables)
usefulness.design_rules_given: Some: friction transfer factors and force comparisons for friction systems, tolerance-chain calculation rules, and properties in the access columns; mostly qualitative for principle selection [uncertain for exact values]
usefulness.generator_or_parametric: No generator; Band 2 describes computer-aided and automatic design of connections using closure matrices and catalogues as software modules (research concepts, no downloadable tool)
usefulness.file_formats: Print and eBook (Springer PDF/EPUB) [uncertain]; VDI guideline as PDF or print
usefulness.terminology_value: high for German design-methodology and machine-element terms (Formschluss, Kraftschluss, Stoffschluss, Ruecklaufsperre, Klemmgesperre, Schlingband, Welle-Nabe-Verbindung, Geradfuehrung, Verschluss), useful for German translations of our entries
usefulness.decision_support: Yes, the whole method is selection: access-part property columns let you filter solutions by required properties, plus evaluation and selection methods (technical-economic evaluation, utility analysis, scales) in Band 2 chapter 12; the 'algorithmic selection procedure' design flow chart in the 1st edition
usefulness.derived_from_or_overlaps: Part of German systematic design (Konstruktionsmethodik) alongside VDI 2221/2222 and the textbooks of Pahl/Beitz and Koller [uncertain]; Band 2 ends with a directory of catalogue and solution collections published by others (section 15.3), making it the best index to other German design catalogues. VDI 2222 Blatt 2 codifies the catalogue structure Roth describes. Its chapter on blocking motion with support points parallels Blanding's exact-constraint design
